task.title: A board view can stay laid over the shell's own message
task.description:
Found by the review of the sidebar-divider fix (2026-10-08); all three predate it and none is changed by it.

1. Failed start over a working board: with board A showing, a failed cold start of board B leaves A's view laid in, so A covers the shell's 'Could not start this board' text and activeProjectId stays A. The user asked for B and sees A with no explanation.
2. Switching away during a slow start: A to B (slow cold start), then a click on Next calls showChrome(), which does not bump openGeneration; when B's open completes it lays B over the Next view and reports a board showing. showChrome() should bump openGeneration so a superseded open parks its view instead.
3. Stopped board: a board whose server stopped keeps its dead page laid in, hiding the 'This board stopped' message beneath it.

In each case the fix is in main.js's openProject/showChrome/supervisor exit handling: park the board view (zero rect) whenever the shell's own project-view content is what the user should see, and send board:showing false then, so the sidebar divider follows. Cover each with a desktop test in the style of divider.test.js and a dev-launch screenshot of the failure text actually visible.
